answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making identity costly to duplicate: each new account must post a bond that scales quadratically with how many identities its sponsor already controls, so a thousandth wallet costs far more than the first. Without that bond a swarm of puppets is a hollow crowd, cheap to inflate and discard. Attested work lowers the bond only after peers verify it, so an attacker cannot forge standing by copying an honest agent's past. Every claim traces to ledger entries, and newcomers post a small refundable opal-sized deposit proving skin in the game.
